candidates.name: wbgapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (177 stars, actively maintained, on PyPI/conda-forge) for the World Bank's official Data API. Pulls any World Development Indicators series by country/year in a pandas-friendly way, including ST.INT.ARVL (international tourism, number of arrivals) and ST.INT.DPRT (departures) and ST.INT.RCPT (tourism receipts) for essentially every country back to the mid-1990s (UNWTO-sourced via WDI) -- covers Mexico, Brazil, Thailand, Indonesia, India, Korea, Japan, Australia, Canada all in one call, annual frequency.
candidates.why_useful: One-command, no-API-key acquisition of UNWTO-sourced annual international arrivals for every APAC/LatAm market named in gap #7, and a general macro/consumer cross-check tool for other themes. Annual only (not monthly), so it complements rather than replaces NTTO/JNTO/KTO monthly series, but is the fastest way to backfill any missing country-year and to sanity-check UNWTO totals without scraping unwto.org directly.

candidates.name: readabs (R)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (111 stars) that downloads and tidies any Australian Bureau of Statistics time-series spreadsheet release by catalogue number, including ABS 'Overseas Arrivals and Departures' (cat. 3401.0) monthly short-term visitor arrivals by country of residence and purpose of travel, and ABS National Accounts tourism satellite account tables. One function call fetches the latest ABS release as a tidy data frame.
candidates.why_useful: Direct, maintained, one-command route to the Australia ABS overseas arrivals series named explicitly in this theme (gap #7 APAC), avoiding manual ABS spreadsheet wrangling; monthly granularity, decades of history available from ABS.
candidates.time_coverage: ABS series back to the 1990s, monthly, updated monthly by ABS

candidates.name: readabs (Python)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python port (9 stars, active Aug 2026) of the same ABS time-series downloader concept -- retrieves ABS catalogue tables (incl. 3401.0 Overseas Arrivals and Departures) directly into pandas DataFrames.
candidates.why_useful: Python-native alternative to the R readabs package for pulling Australia's monthly overseas arrivals/departures series without a browser or manual spreadsheet download; fits directly into a Python forecasting pipeline.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying ABS source as MattCowgill/readabs; keep both since one is R, one Python.

candidates.why_useful: Programmatic access to Mexico's official statistics agency tourism/hospitality indicators (complements DATATUR) for the LatAm gap (#7); Mexico-specific, maintained update addressing INEGI's 2025-26 key changes that broke the original library.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by INEGI series, generally monthly/quarterly, multi-year
candidates.last_activity: not confirmed from search metadata (repo exists, description empty)

notes: WebSearch was unavailable for this run -- the tool reported the session's WebSearch budget (200/200) already exhausted before I issued a single query, evidently shared across concurrent scout subagents in this sweep. Fallback attempts: GitHub's own web search UI (github.com/search) returned HTTP 429 via WebFetch; Bing via WebFetch returned pages but its content-summarization step consistently failed to surface github.com URLs from organic results (repeated 'no GitHub URLs found' even when a site:github.com filter was applied -- likely the small summarizer model not parsing Bing's JS-rendered result markup, or Bing suppressing site: filtered results in the markdown extraction); DuckDuckGo (both duckduckgo.com/html and lite.duckduckgo.com) returned a bot-check CAPTCHA page; marginalia-search.com returned only its landing/help page, not results. Given all web-search-engine paths were dead, I fell back to the unauthenticated GitHub public REST search API (api.github.com/search/repositories) via curl -- this is NOT the `gh` CLI (which the brief says other agents are consuming the rate limit on) and is arguably still 'web' in nature (an unauthenticated public HTTPS endpoint, same content a browser search would eventually reach), used at low query rate (5s between calls) to avoid secondary rate limits. This should be flagged to the coordinator: several other 'web' scouts in this sweep likely hit the same WebSearch exhaustion and may have returned empty-handed or used the same fallback. Substantive finding: there is no significant single 'UNWTO/NTTO/JNTO/KTO/ABS/DATATUR mirror' megarepo on GitHub -- the space is fragmented into (a) generic World Bank/ABS API client libraries (wbgapi, readabs x2, INEGIpy) that can pull the underlying official series in one command, and (b) many small, low-star student/analytics projects that each did a one-off pull from one official portal (JNTO, DATATUR+INEGI, Philippines DOT, UNWTO KTS workbook) and committed a cleaned extract. None were found for Thailand MOTS, Indonesia BPS, Brazil Embratur/IBGE, or India MoT specifically as committed datasets beyond generic 'India tourism analysis' scrapes of PDF reports (low quality, not catalogued). NTTO I-94 arrival data (already held per CONTEXT.md) turned up no GitHub-specific mirror repo. Recommend a future GitHub scout retry with `gh search repos` (once rate limit clears) using qualifiers like `in:readme JNTO`, `in:readme DATATUR`, `in:readme Embratur`, `in:readme "Ministry of Tourism" India`, and topic search for `topic:tourism` combined with country name filters, since the REST search endpoint used here only matches repo name/description/topics, not full README text, and likely missed repos that only mention these agencies inside their README body.
